extra.message: pickle.loads() is called on attacker-controlled input from request.body (or request.GET 'blob', base64-decoded when wrap=b64). pickle deserialization executes arbitrary code during unpickling, yielding remote code execution. The endpoint is reachable via GET (no CSRF required) once the INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate is satisfied.

The 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into an os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) call, allowing OS command injection (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id) and arbitrary command execution. The endpoint is GET-accessible so no CSRF token is needed.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: The user-supplied 'fragment' GET parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. String-constructed Jinja2 templates do not enable autoescaping and allow arbitrary expressions, so an attacker can inject template directives (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[...] }}) leading to server-side template injection and remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: XML from request.body is parsed with lxml etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entity resolution is explicitly enabled, allowing XXE attacks that read local files (file://) or perform SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'lane' GET/POST parameter is passed directly to redirect(lane) with no validation or allow-listing, producing an open redirect that can be abused for phishing (e.g. lane=https://evil.com).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The request Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any malicious origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the JSON responses, a permissive CORS policy that defeats the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() is passed to urllib.request.urlopen, disabling TLS certificate verification for the outbound request. This permits man-in-the-middle attackers to intercept or alter the request/response.

A security-relevant 'code' (the endpoint is named nonce_roll) is generated with the non-cryptographic random module rather than secrets, making the output predictable and unsuitable for security tokens/nonces.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The full request body and the Authorization (bearer) header are written to the application log via logger.warning, exposing credentials/bearer tokens in log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Verifier codes ('4812', '5930') are hardcoded in source for the handle/verifier check. Anyone with access to the code can bypass the verification, and the 4-digit codes are trivially brute-forceable.

The 'elevated' lane (with payroll/casework data) is granted solely based on a client-controlled ops_badge cookie (== 'lead') with no server-side validation. Any caller can set this cookie to escalate to the elevated lane.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string, disabling browser XSS protections and CSP for the endpoint.

course_roster_fold_036 performs no authentication or authorization check (_wrk_gate is not called, unlike the other ops endpoints) and returns internal operational metadata (course counts and an ops memo describing payment flags and owner contact details) to any unauthenticated caller.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for a Critical Function

extra.message: Internal configuration details (the DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable value and the BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path) are returned in the JSON response, leaking implementation details to callers.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: hashlib.md5 is used to produce a digest of user-supplied input. MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash algorithm and must not be used for any security-relevant digesting.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded value 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is absent. A known SECRET_KEY enables forgery of session cookies and CSRF tokens, leading to authentication bypass. There is no check that a strong key is configured.

DEBUG defaults to True (DJANGO_DEBUG defaults to 'True'). If deployed without overriding the env var, Django will render detailed error pages exposing stack traces, settings, and environment data to attackers.

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are not set (default False). Although HttpOnly and SameSite are configured, the session and CSRF cookies can still be transmitted over cleartext HTTP, exposing them to network interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: User-controlled values (assignment titles via sub.assignment.title and student names via sub.student.get_full_name) are written into CSV cells without neutralizing formula characters (=, +, -, @). When the grade export CSV is opened in a spreadsheet, this enables CSV/formula injection.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
